items.question: Why should Project custom instructions be kept to a small, focused set rather than an exhaustive one?

options.A: Longer instruction sets are processed more slowly, increasing response latency
options.B: A large instruction set increases the likelihood of internal contradictions and is harder to maintain and audit
options.C: Instructions beyond a certain count are ignored by Claude to stay within context limits
options.D: Short instruction sets allow Claude to apply more of its context window to knowledge document retrieval

items.question: When should a single large document be split into multiple smaller documents in a Project knowledge base?

options.A: When it exceeds the upload size limit and must be divided to fit
options.B: When it covers multiple distinct topics that are queried independently
options.C: When it was authored by more than one contributor and needs separate attribution
options.D: When it contains images or tables, which must be stored as separate files

items.question: What is the meaningful difference between archiving and deleting a document from a Project knowledge base?

options.A: Archived documents are removed from retrieval but remain accessible to humans for audit; deleted documents are gone entirely
options.B: Archived documents remain in the knowledge base but are ranked lower in retrieval than active documents
options.C: Archiving moves a document to read-only status; deleting removes it and any associated conversation history
options.D: There is no meaningful difference; both actions remove a document from Claude's retrieval context

items.question: Two near-identical documents describing the same process exist in a Project knowledge base. What is the primary quality risk?

options.A: Claude will refuse to retrieve either document and ask the user to resolve the duplication
options.B: Claude may retrieve one copy in one session and the other copy in another, producing inconsistent outputs across the team
options.C: The duplicate will be detected and flagged automatically, preventing it from being stored
options.D: Storage duplication will consume the Project's document quota more quickly

items.question: Which characteristic most precisely distinguishes a Project from a single chat at the product level?

options.A: A Project supports longer conversations before context limits are reached
options.B: A Project provides a shared knowledge base that a single chat does not have
options.C: A Project persists configured instructions and knowledge across all its conversations; a single chat does not carry configuration forward
options.D: A Project can connect to external tools via connectors; a single chat cannot

items.question: Which TWO describe correct uses of the knowledge base and per-chat upload working together in the same Project? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Standing reference material such as a company style guide is stored in the knowledge base; a specific draft document is uploaded per-chat for that session's editing task
options.B: The per-chat upload replaces the knowledge base for that session when both contain documents on the same topic
options.C: A current process document is stored in the knowledge base; a per-chat upload brings in the specific case data that the session's analysis will draw on
options.D: Documents uploaded per-chat are automatically added to the knowledge base at the end of the session for future retrieval
options.E: Uploading a file per-chat creates a temporary version of the knowledge base document that lasts for that session only

items.question: Which TWO are signs that a Project custom instruction is well-written rather than merely long? (Choose TWO)

options.A: It could apply to any Claude Project without modification, demonstrating universal best-practice coverage
options.B: A reader can predict the type of output Claude will produce without needing to run the prompt first
options.C: It covers every possible task variation that might arise in the Project, leaving nothing to the per-chat prompt
options.D: It can be audited in under a minute and contains no phrase that a reasonable reader would interpret in two different ways
options.E: It was reviewed and approved by a manager, ensuring organisational alignment

items.question: Which action is required when an updated policy document is added to a Project knowledge base?

options.A: Delete the new document and wait for all team members to acknowledge the update
options.B: Remove the superseded version so both old and new versions do not coexist
options.C: Rename the old document to indicate it is historical, then keep both in the base
options.D: Archive the entire Project and create a fresh one with only the new document

items.question: What is the primary cause of a knowledge base becoming stale over time?

options.A: Claude periodically purges old documents to free context space
options.B: Documents are added when processes change but outdated versions are not removed
options.C: Connectors stop syncing after a fixed period without manual re-authorisation
options.D: New team members uploading documents gradually overwrite older ones

items.question: Two documents in a Project knowledge base describe the same process with different steps. What is the correct remediation?

options.A: Add a third document that reconciles the two and explains the differences
options.B: Determine which document is authoritative and remove the other
options.C: Tag the documents so Claude knows which to retrieve for which type of query
options.D: Leave both and let Claude decide which to follow based on the specifics of each query

items.question: What should trigger a review of a Project knowledge base's content, in addition to scheduled periodic reviews?

options.A: Each time a team member submits a question using the Project
options.B: Whenever a Claude output references a document by filename
options.C: When a policy, process, or reference document in the underlying organisation changes
options.D: When the Project reaches a defined number of conversations

items.question: What is the primary trade-off when a Project knowledge base grows very large in volume of documents?

options.A: The Project will require a higher-tier subscription to accommodate the additional storage
options.B: Retrieval becomes less precise as more documents compete to match any given query
options.C: Claude switches to a summary-only retrieval mode that reduces response accuracy
options.D: Team members will experience slower response times proportional to the number of documents

items.question: What specific knowledge base problem do connectors solve that static file uploads do not?

options.A: Connectors can store more documents than the per-upload file-count limit allows
options.B: Connectors keep the knowledge base current automatically when the source changes, eliminating manual re-uploads
options.C: Connectors bypass retrieval and inject their content directly into every message
options.D: Connectors grant Claude write access to the source system to update content bi-directionally

items.question: Which signal most clearly indicates that Project custom instructions need revision?

options.A: Claude's responses are consistently longer than expected
options.B: Team members' actual workflow or output standards have changed since the instructions were written
options.C: The Project has accumulated more than a defined number of conversations
options.D: A new team member has been added to the Project

items.question: A reference document is updated monthly. Should it be stored as Project knowledge or uploaded per-chat?

options.A: Per-chat, because monthly updates make it too dynamic to store in a static knowledge base
options.B: Project knowledge, because even monthly updates represent reuse across many sessions
options.C: Per-chat, because Project knowledge cannot be updated; only new documents can be added
options.D: It depends solely on the document's file size

items.question: What is the correct relationship between Project custom instructions and Project knowledge documents?

options.A: Instructions govern behavior; knowledge documents provide reference content — they serve different functions and complement each other
options.B: Knowledge documents override instructions when their content addresses the same topic
options.C: Instructions are processed before knowledge documents and take unconditional precedence
options.D: They are interchangeable; behavioral guidance can be placed in either location with identical effect

items.question: Which type of guidance is most appropriate for Project custom instructions rather than a per-chat prompt?

options.A: A one-time task-specific request that does not apply to any future conversation
options.B: Stable, recurring behavioral requirements that should apply to every conversation in the Project
options.C: A reminder about a specific deadline relevant to today's work only
options.D: Formatting guidance that varies depending on the audience for each individual output

items.question: Which TWO are valid reasons to restrict access to a shared Project rather than making it open to all colleagues? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The Project knowledge base contains commercially sensitive or confidential reference documents
options.B: The Project uses a higher-tier model that should not be available to lower-level staff
options.C: The Project's custom instructions are tuned for a specific team's workflow and are not appropriate for other teams
options.D: Restricting access reduces the number of queries made, lowering usage costs
options.E: The organisation's policy requires all AI tool access to be logged and approved by role

items.question: Which TWO describe safe, correct practices when a per-chat task requires behavior that differs from the standing Project instructions? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Write the per-chat prompt to explicitly request the different behavior, without relying on it to override the instruction
options.B: Temporarily delete the conflicting instruction from the Project before starting the session
options.C: Consider whether the Project instruction needs permanent revision if this new need recurs frequently
options.D: Add a precedence statement to the per-chat prompt declaring it takes priority over all Project instructions
options.E: Use XML tags to mark the per-chat prompt as 'override mode' so Claude processes it first

items.question: Which factor should most influence the decision to use a connector rather than a static file upload for Project knowledge?

options.A: The total size of the content to be made available
options.B: How frequently the source content changes and how critical currency is for the use case
options.C: Whether the content was created by the user or by a third party
options.D: Whether the Project is used individually or shared with a team

items.question: How does a descriptive filename for a knowledge base document affect retrieval quality?

options.A: It increases the document's ranking in retrieval compared to documents with generic filenames
options.B: It helps team members identify and manage documents but does not directly influence Claude's retrieval of document content
options.C: Claude reads filenames as part of the retrieval query and matches them to user questions
options.D: A descriptive filename allows the document to be retrieved without section headings inside the file

items.question: Which scenario does NOT benefit from a Claude Project?

options.A: A team that reviews vendor contracts weekly using the same policy documents and output format
options.B: A researcher who needs a one-off translation of a single document
options.C: A support team that answers customer questions against a shared product knowledge base
options.D: A writer who produces monthly reports following the same brand voice and structure

items.question: What does a persona element in Project custom instructions tell Claude to do?

options.A: Claim to be a human rather than an AI when users ask directly
options.B: Adopt a defined role, expertise level, or voice consistent with the Project's purpose
options.C: Restrict all responses to a specific subject-matter domain, refusing off-topic queries
options.D: Replace the model's default system prompt with the user's custom one

items.question: Who is responsible for the accuracy and currency of documents in a Project knowledge base?

options.A: Anthropic, as the platform provider responsible for content stored on its infrastructure
options.B: The users and team who configure and maintain the Project
options.C: Claude, which flags documents that appear outdated based on its training data
options.D: The organisation's IT department, which manages all data stored in cloud tools

items.question: Why might a very long, unstructured document produce lower retrieval quality than a shorter, well-structured one on the same topic?

options.A: Very long documents are automatically truncated by the knowledge base before storage
options.B: Retrieval must scan more text to identify the relevant section, and without structural anchors it may return a less precise match
options.C: Claude applies a lower confidence score to long documents to account for the greater risk of error
options.D: Long documents consume more context window space per retrieval, reducing the space available for the response

items.question: When is a negative constraint ('do not…') appropriate in Project custom instructions?

options.A: Never; positive framing is always more effective and should replace all negative constraints
options.B: When a specific behavior is important enough to prohibit explicitly and the prohibition is unambiguous
options.C: Only to replace instructions that Claude has demonstrably ignored in positive form
options.D: When the Project is shared with team members who might override instructions per-chat

items.question: How does grounding a response in Project knowledge documents differ from a response drawn from the model's parametric memory?

options.A: Grounded responses are always factually accurate; parametric responses may be incorrect
options.B: Grounded responses trace to material in the knowledge base and can be checked against it; parametric responses cannot be traced to a specific source
options.C: Grounded responses are longer because they quote more source material directly
options.D: Parametric responses are faster because they do not require retrieval from the knowledge base

items.question: What consistency risk does a shared Project with team-level custom instructions primarily address?

options.A: Team members using different model tiers and producing outputs at different quality levels
options.B: Individual team members writing their own prompts differently, producing outputs that vary in format, tone, and standards
options.C: Claude producing different responses for the same prompt across different sessions
options.D: Team members accidentally deleting each other's conversation histories

items.question: A single document contains both an expense policy and a travel booking procedure. When should it be split into two documents?

options.A: Always; all knowledge base documents should cover exactly one topic
options.B: Only when the combined document exceeds the upload size limit
options.C: When users are likely to query the expense policy and the travel procedure independently of each other
options.D: When the two sections were authored by different people and require separate attribution

items.question: A team wants Claude to always apply a five-step review checklist. Where should this checklist be placed?

options.A: In a knowledge document titled 'Review Checklist', so Claude can retrieve it when asked to review
options.B: In the Project custom instructions, with a directive to apply it to every review task
options.C: In the per-chat prompt, where it can be tailored for each specific review
options.D: As a comment inside a template document, so Claude reads it when the template is submitted

items.question: Which scenario describes an instruction conflict that is most likely to produce unpredictable outputs?

options.A: One instruction specifies a formal tone; a per-chat prompt requests a casual summary for an internal audience
options.B: Two Project instructions both address the same situation but specify different behaviors
options.C: A knowledge document contains information that contradicts a per-chat question's premise
options.D: An instruction uses a technical term that is not defined elsewhere in the instructions

items.question: A Project knowledge base is authoritative but silent on a topic a user asks about. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: Claude refuses the query, citing that the knowledge base does not cover this topic
options.B: Claude draws on its parametric memory to answer, which may or may not be accurate for this organisation's specific context
options.C: Claude retrieves the most closely related knowledge base document and summarises it instead
options.D: Claude asks the user to upload a relevant document before proceeding

items.question: Which TWO practices make a Project's instructions and knowledge documents work together most effectively? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Instructions reference knowledge documents by name, directing Claude to apply them for specific task types
options.B: Knowledge documents contain all behavioral guidance, with instructions left blank to avoid redundancy
options.C: Instructions govern how Claude behaves; knowledge documents supply the reference material Claude draws on when behaving that way
options.D: Instructions and knowledge documents are kept identical in content to ensure Claude receives consistent signals
options.E: Knowledge documents are structured with clear headings so retrieval can surface the right section when instructions direct Claude to consult them

items.question: When should a Claude Project be retired rather than updated in place?

options.A: When the Project has accumulated more conversations than the platform supports
options.B: When the underlying workflow the Project was built for no longer exists or has been replaced by a fundamentally different one
options.C: When the Project has been shared with more than a defined number of team members
options.D: When a new Claude model version is released that requires a fresh Project configuration

items.question: Which TWO risks arise when sensitive or confidential documents are added to a widely shared Project knowledge base? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Users with Project access can ask Claude questions that surface content from those documents in responses
options.B: Claude will automatically redact sensitive content when serving responses to lower-privileged users
options.C: Sensitive content retrieved into responses may be copied, shared, or exported by Project users
options.D: The sensitive documents will be indexed by external search engines through the Project's public URL
options.E: The project will be flagged by Anthropic's trust and safety systems and suspended

items.question: How does adding accurate reference documents to a Project knowledge base reduce fabrication risk?

options.A: It prevents Claude from accessing its parametric memory for any topic covered in the documents
options.B: It provides grounding material Claude can retrieve and cite instead of generating from parametric memory
options.C: It triggers a verification step where Claude cross-checks its output against the documents before responding
options.D: It replaces the model's knowledge for that domain with the uploaded content, improving factual accuracy

items.question: What is the recommended approach to Project custom instruction length?

options.A: As long as necessary to cover every possible scenario the Project might encounter
options.B: As short as possible while remaining specific enough to produce consistent, predictable outputs
options.C: Exactly ten or fewer instructions, regardless of Project complexity
options.D: Long enough that team members can infer the Project's purpose without reading the Project name

items.question: What is the primary purpose of periodically auditing a Project knowledge base?

options.A: To measure Claude's retrieval accuracy against a benchmark set of test queries
options.B: To identify and remove outdated, duplicate, or out-of-scope documents before they degrade output quality
options.C: To verify that all documents are stored in a supported file format
options.D: To check that the Project's usage has not exceeded the knowledge base storage quota

items.question: Which type of document should NOT be added to a Project knowledge base?

options.A: A style guide that the team references for every deliverable
options.B: A transcript of a specific meeting that will not be referenced again after today
options.C: An approved-supplier policy updated quarterly and needed in every vendor review
options.D: A glossary of technical terms used across all Project outputs

items.question: What makes a format instruction in Project custom instructions effective?

options.A: It specifies the desired output structure precisely — for example, a specific number of sections, headings, or list items
options.B: It references a sample output Claude can use as a style template
options.C: It uses markdown formatting within the instruction text itself to demonstrate the expected format
options.D: It names the format (e.g., 'executive summary') and relies on Claude to apply the conventional structure

items.question: When is putting all reference material into a Project knowledge base preferable to including it all directly in a long per-chat context?

options.A: When the reference material changes frequently and different sessions need different subsets of it
options.B: When the total reference material is too large to fit into a single chat context
options.C: When speed is the primary concern and shorter contexts process faster
options.D: When only a subset of the reference material is relevant to any given query and selective retrieval is more efficient

items.question: A team lead wants all staff outputs to include a standard disclaimer. What is the most reliable configuration approach?

options.A: Train staff to include the disclaimer in every per-chat prompt
options.B: Upload the disclaimer as a knowledge base document titled 'Disclaimer'
options.C: Include the disclaimer text and an instruction to always include it in the Project custom instructions
options.D: Ask staff to append the disclaimer manually after each Claude output

items.question: Why does terminology consistency across knowledge base documents improve retrieval quality?

options.A: Consistent terminology prevents Claude from generating synonyms that might confuse the user
options.B: Query terms are more likely to match document text when both use the same terminology, improving retrieval precision
options.C: Inconsistent terminology causes a validation error that prevents documents from being stored
options.D: Consistent terminology enables Claude to rank documents by relevance more effectively than synonym matching can

items.question: How do well-written Project custom instructions reduce the onboarding effort for a new team member?

options.A: They train the new team member on the organisation's AI use policy automatically through the Project interface
options.B: They encode the team's standards in the Project so the new member gets consistent outputs without needing to learn every prompting convention individually
options.C: They prevent the new team member from modifying the Project configuration until approved
options.D: They generate an onboarding guide for the new member based on the Project's knowledge documents

items.question: A Project instruction says outputs must be in formal English. A knowledge document is written in informal language. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: Claude refuses to retrieve the informal document because it conflicts with the format instruction
options.B: Claude retrieves the informal document but reformulates its response in formal English as instructed
options.C: The instruction is overridden by the document's tone once the document is retrieved
options.D: The conflict causes Claude to request clarification before generating a response

items.question: A Project knowledge base was originally built for contract review but now contains HR policy, travel guidelines, and team meeting notes. What compound problem does this represent?

options.A: Scope creep combined with accumulation without curation, degrading retrieval precision for the original use case
options.B: A misconfigured connector that is pulling in unrelated content from linked systems
options.C: A permissions problem allowing unauthorised team members to add documents
options.D: Normal growth of a knowledge base as a team's needs evolve over time

items.question: Which TWO describe situations where updating the Project's custom instructions is more appropriate than adjusting the per-chat prompt? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A format standard changes and will now apply to all future work in the Project, not just the current task
options.B: Today's task requires a longer word limit than the instruction currently specifies
options.C: A recurring tone requirement that every team member needs for all their Project conversations
options.D: A one-time exception to include additional context for a specific high-stakes output
options.E: A task that requires a specific file format not normally produced by this Project

items.question: Which event most clearly signals that a document should be removed from a Project knowledge base?

options.A: The document has not been retrieved in the past month
options.B: The process or policy the document describes has been officially superseded or retired
options.C: A newer document on a different topic has been added to the knowledge base
options.D: The document's author has left the organisation

items.question: Which TWO scenarios most justify using a connector rather than a static file upload for Project knowledge? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A product pricing table updated weekly that is referenced in every customer proposal
options.B: A foundational company history document unchanged for three years
options.C: A team wiki page actively edited by multiple contributors that serves as the reference for all Project outputs
options.D: A regulatory compliance checklist reviewed and updated annually
options.E: A glossary of acronyms created once and expected to be stable indefinitely

items.question: A user needs Claude's help for a single exploratory brainstorming session with no planned follow-up. What is the appropriate surface?

options.A: A new Project with minimal instructions to allow flexible thinking
options.B: A plain single chat — no Project overhead is warranted for a one-off session
options.C: An existing Project with broad instructions that approximates the topic
options.D: A new Project with no instructions, used only for exploratory work
